newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chevron Nigeria takes delivery of gas vessel.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Nigeria takes delivery of gas vessel.

text.p: Chevron Nigeria Ltd said it took delivery on Thursday of a gas storage vessel for its Escravos gas project which was the first of its kind in the world.

The floating storage and offloading (FSO) facility was taken over from the manufacturers, Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co. Ltd at a ceremony at the company's shipyard at Nagoya, Japan, Chevron said in a statement in Lagos.

The Escravos gas project is being executed by the Chevron Nigeria Ltd, a joint venture between Chevron Corp and state-run Nigeria National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) to reduce gas flaring and recover gas and condensate from two of its oil fields.

It is to come on stream in May 1997 and will process 165 million cubic feet of associated gas daily into condensates and liquefied petroleum gas for export via the FSO and natural gas for distribution to industry users in Nigeria.
Chevron said following the successful building of the FSO, the vessel would now undergo LPG trials in Japan before being towed to Nigeria for installation and commissioning next May.
The Chevron-NNPC joint venture pumps about 400,000 barrels per day of crude oil, most of it from offshore fields in the Escravos area of the midwestern Delta state.
